# A396102 and the inverse-iterate family

**Result.** The conjecture in [OEIS A396102](https://oeis.org/A396102) is true: every positive-index coefficient of its generating function is congruent to 1 modulo 3. The Lean proof constructs the generating function over the integers, proves its original functional equation and uniqueness, and establishes the congruence for every positive index.

**AI disclosure.** This proof, its Lean formalization, this explanation, and the independent numerical checks were generated by OpenAI ChatGPT for Dev Goyal. See the package's `AI_DISCLOSURE.md` for the complete attribution and limitations. Kernel verification certifies the stated formal theorems; it does not certify historical novelty.

## Source statement and scope

The OEIS entry defines a normalized formal power series

\[
A(x)=x+\sum_{n\ge2}a(n)x^n
\]

by

\[
A\bigl(A(A(x))\bigr)=(1+x)A(A(x)).
\tag{1}
\]

Its displayed conjecture is \(a(n)\equiv1\pmod3\) for every \(n\ge1\). The same entry supplies the equivalent inverse formulation \(R(x)=x/(1+R^{\circ3}(x))\), where \(R=A^{-1}\) is the compositional inverse. Both the original equation and the inverse formulation appear in [A396102, formulas (1), (4), and (5)](https://oeis.org/A396102), checked on 24 October 2026.

Here \(G^{\circ j}\) always means composition repeated \(j\) times, with \(G^{\circ0}(x)=x\). Ordinary multiplication and ordinary powers are written separately. The normalization includes both zero constant term and linear coefficient one.

The proof gives the following generalization. For each integer \(r\ge1\), there is a unique normalized integral series \(F_r\) satisfying

\[
F_r^{\circ r}(x)=(1+x)F_r^{\circ(r-1)}(x).
\tag{2}
\]

For every \(n\ge1\),

\[
[x^n]F_r(x)\equiv1\pmod r.
\tag{3}
\]

More generally, for every \(k\ge0\) and \(n\ge1\),

\[
[x^n]F_r^{\circ k}(x)\equiv k^{n-1}\pmod r.
\tag{4}
\]

The convention \(0^0=1\) makes (4) include the identity iterate \(k=0\). The parameter \(r=1\) gives \(F_1=x+x^2\), with congruences modulo one interpreted in the usual way. The formal auxiliary construction also admits parameter zero; the original-equation theorem (2) is stated only for positive parameters. A396102 is exactly \(F_3\).

## 1. An integral canonical construction

Work first over any commutative ring \(S\). For a normalized series \(G\), define

\[
\Phi_r(G)=x-GG^{\circ r}.
\]

The product begins in degree two, so \(\Phi_r(G)\) is normalized. Moreover, if

\[
G\equiv H\pmod{x^N},
\]

then substitution and repeated composition preserve that congruence:

\[
G^{\circ r}\equiv H^{\circ r}\pmod{x^N}.
\]

The difference of products can be written as

\[
GG^{\circ r}-HH^{\circ r}
=(G-H)G^{\circ r}+H(G^{\circ r}-H^{\circ r}).
\]

Both \(G^{\circ r}\) and \(H\) are divisible by \(x\), including the case \(r=0\). Thus

\[
\Phi_r(G)\equiv\Phi_r(H)\pmod{x^{N+1}}.
\tag{5}
\]

This strict increase in the degree of agreement constructs a unique normalized fixed point \(R_r\):

\[
R_r=x-R_rR_r^{\circ r}.
\tag{6}
\]

Concretely, its coefficient of degree \(n\ge2\) is the negative of the degree-\(n\) coefficient of \(R_rR_r^{\circ r}\), which depends only on coefficients of degrees less than \(n\). This is a triangular recurrence using only addition and multiplication. There is no division and no assumption that an integral solution already exists.

In Lean, `R_exists` proves the existence of this fixed point with the previously verified triangular-recursion machinery. `R_unique` derives uniqueness from (5). `R` is then the chosen actual power series whose existence and uniqueness have been proved.

Every normalized series has a unique normalized compositional inverse over the same coefficient ring, because the coefficient of the unknown next inverse coefficient is one. Define

\[
F_r=R_r^{-1}.
\tag{7}
\]

The existing formal reversion construction proves both identities \(R_r\circ F_r=x\) and \(F_r\circ R_r=x\). In particular, constructing \(R_r\) over \(\mathbb Z\) gives an actual integral \(F_r\).

## 2. Equivalence with the original equation

Rewrite (6) as

\[
R_r(1+R_r^{\circ r})=x.
\tag{8}
\]

Substitute \(F_r^{\circ r}\) into (8). Repeated forward and inverse composition cancel, giving

\[
(R_r\circ F_r^{\circ r})
\bigl(1+R_r^{\circ r}\circ F_r^{\circ r}\bigr)
=F_r^{\circ r}.
\]

The two factors on the left become \(F_r^{\circ(r-1)}\) and \(1+x\), respectively. This proves (2).

Conversely, suppose a normalized series \(G\) satisfies (2), and let \(H=G^{-1}\). Substituting \(H^{\circ r}\) into that equation gives

\[
x=(1+H^{\circ r})H,
\]

because \(G^{\circ(r-1)}\circ H^{\circ r}=H\). Hence \(H=x-HH^{\circ r}\). Uniqueness of the fixed point in (6) gives \(H=R_r\), and uniqueness of compositional inversion gives \(G=F_r\).

Therefore the canonical construction satisfies exactly the original defining equation, and every normalized series satisfying that equation is the constructed one. The argument proves both directions; the modular theorem is not conditional on an unproved existence or identification claim.

The Lean statement `F_original_existence_uniqueness` uses \(r+1\) to express a positive parameter without natural-number subtraction. At parameter three, `a396102_definition` states the literal threefold-composition equation (1), and `a396102_unique` proves its uniqueness.

## 3. Reduction modulo the parameter

Coefficient reduction commutes with composition, the fixed-point construction, and compositional inversion. For the fixed point this follows by mapping equation (6) and applying uniqueness over the target ring; for inversion it follows from the two inverse identities and their uniqueness.

For a scalar \(c\), put

\[
M_c(x)=\frac{x}{1-cx}.
\]

All quotients here are formal power series with unit constant denominator. A direct composition calculation gives

\[
M_a\circ M_b=M_{a+b},\qquad M_c^{\circ k}=M_{kc},\qquad M_c^{-1}=M_{-c}.
\tag{9}
\]

Now work in \((\mathbb Z/r\mathbb Z)[[x]]\). For \(Q=M_{-1}=x/(1+x)\), equation (9) gives

\[
Q^{\circ r}=M_{-r}=M_0=x.
\]

Consequently,

\[
x-QQ^{\circ r}=x-xQ=Q.
\]

Thus \(Q\) is a normalized fixed point of the same operator as the reduction of \(R_r\). Uniqueness gives

\[
R_r\equiv M_{-1}\pmod r,
\qquad
F_r=R_r^{-1}\equiv M_1=\frac{x}{1-x}\pmod r.
\tag{10}
\]

Every positive coefficient of the final series is one, proving (3). For the iterates, (9) yields

\[
F_r^{\circ k}\equiv M_k
=\frac{x}{1-kx}
=\sum_{n\ge1}k^{n-1}x^n\pmod r,
\]

which proves (4). Setting \(r=3\) proves the conjecture in A396102.

## Formal endpoints and verification

The complete formalization is in `lean/More/InverseIterate.lean`.

| Lean declaration | Verified content |
|---|---|
| `R_existence_uniqueness` | Unique normalized fixed point of the integral auxiliary equation |
| `F_original_existence_uniqueness` | Existence and uniqueness for the original functional equation, for every positive parameter |
| `map_R`, `map_F` | Coefficient maps preserve the constructed series and its true inverse |
| `R_mod`, `F_mod` | Exact equalities of reduced formal power series |
| `coefficient_congruence` | Every positive coefficient of \(F_r\) is 1 modulo \(r\) |
| `a396102_definition` | Literal OEIS threefold-composition equation |
| `a396102_unique` | Every normalized solution of the OEIS equation is the constructed A396102 |
| `a396102_congruence` | The OEIS conjecture for every positive index |
| `iterate_coefficient_congruence` | Formula (4) for every natural iterate and positive coefficient index |

The module compiled successfully with Lean 4.19.0 and the package's pinned Mathlib revision. An explicit axiom audit of the source-equation existence/uniqueness, literal definition, uniqueness, conjecture, and iterate theorem reported only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. These are the standard logical axioms used by the Mathlib development; there are no added mathematical axioms, admitted proofs, or trusted native-computation shortcuts in this module.

Independent exact-integer computations are provided by `tests/check_inverse_iterate.py`, with results in `validation/inverse_iterate_checks.json`. The default check constructs degrees 0 through 40 for parameters 1 through 8, verifies both inverse identities and the literal original equation, checks every congruence in (3), and checks (4) for iterates 0 through 8. It also compares all 23 coefficients displayed in the official A396102 entry, not merely their residues. These finite computations check implementation and source identification; the Lean theorems provide the all-index proof.

To reproduce the finite checks from the package root:

```sh
python tests/check_inverse_iterate.py
```

To check the formal module from `lean/`:

```sh
lake build More.InverseIterate
```

## Historical qualifications

The official A396102 entry retrieved on 24 October 2026 still labels its residue statement a conjecture and gives no proof reference. An exact-number search did not reveal an indexed proof. This documents the source status checked for this package; it does not establish worldwide novelty or priority. The family theorem above is presented as a proved extension within this package, without a claim that no equivalent result exists elsewhere.

The different positive-iterate family \(A=x+xA^{\circ\ell}\) must not be counted as a new result here: [OEIS A196523](https://oeis.org/A196523) records a general proof of its modulo-\(\ell-1\) coefficient congruence by Amol Bhave, dated 13 October 2026. That prior theorem covers A378575 and A378576 even though their individual entries retained conjecture labels when checked. The present family uses the inverse equation (6) and the source equation (2), with its own integral construction and verification.
